Figure 2:Overview of the OS-Helix pipeline.Stage 1constructs executable desktop environments by composing applications and artifacts.Stage 2explores each environment to synthesize instructions and evaluators, yielding verifiable tasks.Stage 3uses teacher-generated GUI/code trajectories for SFT cold start.Stage 4performs online agentic RL in live sandboxes.

Figure 6:Successful GUI–code coordination cases. The top case first uses GUI observation to infer the URL pattern from an opened lecture slide, then uses code to download the remaining weekly PDFs. The bottom case uses code to extract payment records from a spreadsheet and then returns to the GUI to fill the e-mail recipients.

Figure 7:Successful cross-modality solve-and-verify cases. The top case creates a spreadsheet chart with code and then detects from the GUI that one data series is missing before repairing it. The bottom case completes slide editing through GUI actions and then verifies the saved file with code.

Figure 8:Representative failure cases.Top:In a Calc-to-Writer transfer task requiring preservation of the original formatting, code-based conversion fails to retain the alternating row shading. The subsequent GUI observation identifies a mismatch but misattributes it to missing currency symbols, so the agent adds dollar signs instead of restoring the table style.Bottom:After correctly completing the first PowerPoint subgoal through GUI actions, the agent edits and saves the second with code. The code-side save does not include the unsaved GUI state, and selecting “Don’t Save” subsequently discards the earlier update.
